title: Primary current relation
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (1) must correctly apply the transformer turns ratio to give I_0 = I/n.

title: Motor electrical power
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (2) must correctly calculate the motor's input power as P = U_2 * I, leading to the form (√2 * U_0 * I) / (2n).

title: Constant speed condition
description: Important: The student must recognize that at constant speed, the motor's useful mechanical power equals the rate of work against gravity, P_mech = mgv.

title: Energy conservation step
description: Important: The student must subtract the Joule heating loss (I²R) from the total electrical power to find the useful mechanical power.

title: RMS voltage application
description: Important: The student must correctly relate the peak source voltage U_0 to the RMS secondary voltage using U_2 = U_0 / (√2 n).

title: Final velocity expression
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (3) must combine all previous steps into the correct algebraic expression for v.

title: Sign or ratio reversal
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the transformer current or voltage ratio is inverted (e.g., I_0 = nI or U_2 = nU).

title: Ignoring motor resistance
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the calculation for velocity uses the total electrical power (P) instead of the net mechanical power (P - I²R).
